content: Cross-post: In #lean4lean > modelling nested inductives I describe ongoing work to make con-leche handle nested inductives directly, not via a Lean model. (To avoid confusion: the current way is roundabout, but still verified. That work is to have something more satisfying, but both approaches are consistent.)

Update

  • con-leche no longer relies on modelling inductives. It now handles all inductives, even mutual and nested uniformly, with an extended positivity checker. See #lean4lean > modelling nested inductives for more details. (For nested inductives this was somewhat hard, not quite but close to the the rest of con-leche. For simple inductives, where we have had this for 2 weeks now, however, it was very easy.)

    (con-ron sync is pending, should be done soon.)

This approach, of first making a minimal, provably consistent kernel, and then improving it (Rust translation, verified bignum, faster, no more modeling inductives, etc…) has really paid off! I look forward to what’s next.

Question: How much does this approach match the current treatment of mutual inductives? Are there key differences, especially proofs that would/wouldn’t be accepted by your approach but wouldn’t/would be by the default kernel? In particular, one thing I noticed when I looked into this are Projections from Prop structures with data fields (mentioned in lean4#7637). I think I saw that these didn’t follow from the inductive models (and maybe for good reasons).

I had Claude work on a proof that the official’s treatment of nested inductives implies that my positivity checker accepts it. It got far, but there were some corner cases (my checker replaces inductives with “holes”, fvars, and that may potentially affect whnf’ing, and then things get complicated). I may get back to that experiment, we’ll see.

Cross post: I tried to extract the core idea of the consistency proof, in case someone is curious: https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/621470-lean4lean/topic/con-leche.20proof.20idea.20write.20up/with/628933055

Updates

  • Anticipating more and more multi-million-loc proofs, I worked on better parallelism in con-leche. The parser and env-building (the “installer”) phase are now also multi-threaded. Good results (this is on mathlib, 32 threads):

 │ (median, min–max) │  before (d0fff574b)   │ after (01ff6bfe1)  │ speed-up │

 │ wall              │ 146.1 s (126.6–198.4) │ 53.1 s (47.6–75.3) │ 2.75×    │
 ├───────────────────┼───────────────────────┼────────────────────┼──────────┤
 │ parse             │ 30.9 s (22.7–48.3)    │ 8.2 s (3.9–20.9)   │ 3.8×     │
 ├───────────────────┼───────────────────────┼────────────────────┼──────────┤
 │ install           │ 64.2 s (54.5–83.5)    │ 4.3 s (3.9–7.6)    │ 15×      │
 ├───────────────────┼───────────────────────┼────────────────────┼──────────┤
 │ check             │ 50.2 s (46.9–64.1)    │ 40.6 s (38.7–45.1) │ 1.24×    │
 ├───────────────────┼───────────────────────┼────────────────────┼──────────┤
 │ peak RSS          │ 6.57 GiB              │ 7.17 GiB           │ +9 %     │
 └───────────────────┴───────────────────────┴────────────────────┴──────────┘

  • More perf statistics shown at the end of the run

  • Changes to the defeq heuristics to closer match what the official kernel does. By Hyrum’s law, for every checker that is less lazy during defeq or whnf than the official kernel there seems to be some proof that explodes in time or space in that checker.

Update

This is a big one (for me at least):

I found a way to do the consistency proof without these extra annotations on Expr, so con-leche now runs on an expression type that is essentially the same as that of every other checker out there. The remaining behavior difference over other checkers that is needed to get the proof through as a few extra calls to infer/defeq in in the congruence and eta rule for ∀, and ι for large elim Props (Quot, Acc, PUnit). So this moves the checker and its proof much closer to the official checker. (More on the changes to the proof in over at #lean4lean > con-leche proof idea write up ).

This also makes the checker faster and slimmer:

mathlib-full, --verified --jobs=32:

before after
wall time 45.1 s 36.8 s −18 %
parse phase 3.8 s 3.85 s ±0
install phase 3.9 s 2.65 s −32 %
check phase 35.8 s 30.1 s −16 %
peak RSS 7.4 GiB 5.4 GiB −27 %

Single-threaded, mathlib-full needs 7.05 T instructions, against 10.26 T for the official kernel (0.69×).
